doc: The Granary Riot (slug granary-riot) - slot 3 of the master-everyday batch (THR-1688).
Brief: `Docs/plans/encounters/master-everyday-brief.md`.
Final: `Docs/plans/encounters/granary-riot-final.md`. Package critic: `granary-riot-package.md`.
plotHookRolled: hook.civil_unrest, hook.relic_awakening, hook.the_great_building
plotHookTaken:  hook.civil_unrest - a town turning on its own institution over bread. The Great Building
survives as the question underneath it: whose winter pays for whose spring.
Seed dice: p3 plea - opposition beast (territory), read as a frightened crowd (brief override) -
disposition open - agentRole judge_asked_to_rule - scale settlement - system cards.
--- The narrator's 12 questions, answered ---
1 P1 arrival?      Yes: {actor} arrives at {location} in the morning. Graph names.
2 P2 events?       Bread doubled overnight; a crowd is pushing at the abbey granary's gate; two people are
already hurt (cost paid); the abbot will not open it because the grain is next year's seed.
3 P3 one stake?    Plea (rolled): {cast:speaker} and the abbey's cellarer both ask {actor} to rule on the grain,
and first to talk the crowd back before the gate gives.
4 <=80 words?      78 by the gate (opening + step-0 spine).
5 Read aloud?      Report throughout; no interior sensation, no camera work.
6 Stated?          "The abbot will not open it." "The grain inside is the abbey's seed for next year."
7 Every sentence works? Challenge, test or outcome.
8 Nothing unintroduced? Crowd, gate, bar, key, seed, speaker and cellarer are in the spines before the hands.
9 One named person? Step 0 names {cast:speaker}; step 1 names {cast:cellarer}; the abbot is a role noun.
10 Stake in a sentence? Can {actor} hold a hungry crowd back from the abbey granary and name a share of the
grain that both the crowd and the abbey accept?
11 Cards verb+noun? Calm Frightened People, Hold The Gate, Remember Lean Years, Open Closed Hands.
12 Opening per class? urban, written.
--- Mechanical design block ---
Crux            A hungry crowd is forcing the abbey granary's gate, and both the crowd and the abbey ask
{actor} to rule how much grain leaves it.
Shape           Danger - Confrontation - Aftermath. heart 0.76 (continue_weakened) -> heart 0.80
(fail_action). Linear, branch count 0. Mean 0.78, window fit 0.92 (master).
Consequence hand (binding): relationship + story_seed, no swap.
relationship - bond_change with $cast:speaker and $cast:cellarer on both sides of step 1,
and with $cast:cellarer on step 0 failure (the gate gave way on the abbey's watch).
story_seed - placeless encounter_seed query #watch_errand on step 1 success: a town watch
hears how the mortal settled the granary and has work for them.
Standing        reputation_with $here +0.06 on step 1 success, -0.06 on step 1 failure, -0.02 on step 0
failure (backs the critical_failure chip on both routes: a critical failure at either step
ends the action).
Chips (THR-1685) Person bond chips use the plain noun `reputation` anchored on the cast member, no
{target}. The only `reputation with {location}` chips are anchored on $here.
Reactions       Failure-side reactions held at +/-0.04 so no band chip is false after either pick.
Tone            Ends warm on the success side: the crowd goes home with bread and the abbey keeps its seed.
Cool failure    Nobody dies, is jailed or branded. Failure is the master's name: people send for a master
because a master's word ends quarrels, and neither side took this one's.
Cost channels   All specials essence-priced except the Warm trait card (cost 0). No Heavy Hand, no rider,
no grants, no over-exposed library card as a special.
Expert collision The Heart experts are feud_mediation (make peace) and inheritance_wake (settle a will);
this verb is hold back a crowd, then apportion a store.
Accepted limit  The #watch_errand query keeps the family eligibility filter, so the sequel withers if the
mortal is outside a town, city or capital when it ripens. The chip claims only that word
reaches a town watch.
--- Trait hooks (mandatory four questions) ---
Gate? No - everyday board, no rule gates by brief. Variant? Yes - Warm (trait.core.core_warmth.virtue)
+0.04 and Cold (trait.core.core_warmth.vice) -0.04. Trait-only nudge? Yes - granary.open_closed_hands on
step 1, cost 0, unlocked by the Warm variant. Trait fragment? The trait card's own band fragments.
--- Hands ---
Step 0: Whisper (mind, Calm Frightened People) + Boost (force, Hold The Gate), deal 3 presence/peril.
Step 1: Omen (time, Remember Lean Years) + Trait card (Warm, Open Closed Hands), deal 3 presence/social.
Editorial loop 1 REVISE (opening contradiction, passive danger act, carryover/afterimage echoes, band-page
repetition, reaction magnitudes) -> redraft -> editorial loop 2 PASS WITH REVISIONS. Systems READY FOR
IMPLEMENTATION (S1-S5: seed chip promise, three rule-7b overview fixes, person chip anchors). Package PASS
(connected).

template.name: The Granary Riot

steps.narrativeTemplate:
Bread doubled in price overnight. A crowd is pushing at the abbey granary's gate, and two people are already hurt. The abbot will not open it. The grain inside is the abbey's seed for next year.

{cast:speaker} speaks for the crowd, and the abbey's cellarer for the abbey. Both ask {actor} to rule how much grain leaves the granary. First {actor} must talk the crowd back before the gate gives.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: The crowd stepped back from the gate and sat down to wait.
steps.successAfterimage: The crowd stepped back from the gate and fell quiet.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: The crowd stepped back, but not before the gate bar cracked under their weight.
steps.failureAfterimage: The crowd forced the gate and carried sacks out before {cast:speaker} turned them back.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: The crowd broke the gate down and poured into the granary.

nudges.name: Calm Frightened People
nudges.effectLine: Take the panic out of a crowd, so those at the front stop pushing and start to listen.

bandProse.critical_success: The pushing stopped at the front first, and then all the way back to the street.
bandProse.success: The people at the front stopped pushing and turned to listen.
bandProse.near_miss: The front of the crowd grew calm, but the back kept pushing for a while.
bandProse.failure: The people at the front grew calm, and the people behind pushed them into the gate anyway.

nudges.name: Hold The Gate
nudges.effectLine: Make a door or bar bear far more weight than it was built for, so it stands a while longer.

bandProse.success: The gate bar bowed under the crowd's weight and did not break.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The hinges held the gate shut after the bar gave way.
bandProse.failure: The bar held, and the hinges tore out of the wall instead.
bandProse.critical_failure: The gate held until it fell flat into the yard all at once.

steps.narrativeTemplate: Now {actor} must rule, in front of the crowd and the abbey. {cast:cellarer} holds the granary key, and says every sack given away now is a field unsown next spring. The crowd's speaker says the town will not reach spring without bread. The ruling has to be one both sides accept.
steps.criticalSuccessAfterimage: Both sides took the ruling. The cellarer opened the gate, and the crowd cheered {actor}.
steps.successAfterimage: Both sides took the ruling, and the cellarer opened the gate.
steps.successAtCostAfterimage: Both sides took the ruling, but the cellarer argued over every sack.
steps.failureAfterimage: Neither side would take the ruling. The cellarer locked the gate, and the crowd went home hungry.
steps.criticalFailureAfterimage: Neither side would take the ruling, and the crowd broke into the granary.

critical_success.text: The crowd trusts the judge to be fair.

success.text: The crowd is willing to hear the judge out.

success_at_cost.text: The cellarer is angry about the damage to the gate.

near_miss.text: The crowd stepped back late, and is still angry.

failure.text: The abbey is already short of seed, and angry about it.

effects.seedLabel: A town watch has heard how {actor} settled the granary, and has work for them.

nudges.name: Remember Lean Years
nudges.effectLine: Bring back a hungry winter everyone listening lived through, so they weigh tomorrow's hunger against today's.

bandProse.critical_success: Old people in the crowd spoke of the spring the seed was eaten, and the young ones listened.
bandProse.success: An old weaver in the crowd remembered the spring with no seed to sow, and said so.
bandProse.success_at_cost: The crowd remembered the lean spring, but only the old ones would settle for less.
bandProse.near_miss: The crowd remembered the hungry winter, but only after it had refused the first ruling.
bandProse.failure: The crowd remembered a hungry winter, and judged this one worse.
bandProse.critical_failure: The crowd remembered the last hungry winter, and would not wait to starve through another.

nudges.name: Open Closed Hands
nudges.effectLine: Wake their care for others, so everyone listening believes they mind who goes hungry, and each side gives a little.

bandProse.success: {actor} spoke as one who cares who eats, and the crowd believed it.
bandProse.failure: {actor} plainly cared who ate, and the cellarer called that soft.

traitVariants.factorLine: Being Warm, they can make a hungry crowd believe they care.
Being Cold, they cannot make a hungry crowd believe they care.

narrativeTemplates.initiation: A hungry crowd is at the abbey granary gate, and both sides send for a judge to rule on the grain.

narrativeTemplates.failure: The ruling failed, and the granary stayed shut against a hungry town.

template.description: A two-step master Heart job in a town: bread has doubled overnight and a crowd is forcing the abbey granary gate. The mortal holds the crowd back, then rules before the abbey and the crowd on how much of the abbey's seed grain leaves the granary. A ruling both sides accept wins the trust of the crowd's speaker and the abbey's cellarer, raises the mortal's standing with the town and plants a town-watch errand; a refused ruling costs both and the town's regard.
